svg.text: Phosphorylation adds a bulky −2 charge to serine
Phosphate pKa₂ ≈ 5.8, so at pH 7.4 about 98% is the −2 form. α-carbon stays S (no stereo change).
New electrostatic contacts: the phosphate pairs with Arg/Lys (+) and repels Asp/Glu (−),
so loops and domains rearrange. Example: glycogen phosphorylase b → a; many kinase
activation loops. Phosphatases remove the phosphate, making it a reversible switch.
